title: Switchable Acoustic and Optical Resolution Photoacoustic Microscopy for In Vivo Small-animal Blood Vasculature Imaging
protocol: Use a nanosecond tunable laser system consisting of a diode-pumped, solid-state Nd-YAG laser (532 nm) and a dye laser with a tunability range of 559-576 nm as the optical irradiation source.
Set the laser wavelength to 570 nm using an external controller.
Set the repetition rate of the laser to 1 kHz using the laser software.
Place a beam sampler at a 45° angle in front of the laser.
Divert 5% of the laser power to a photodiode through a variable neutral density filter (NDF1; OD = 0-4.0).
Divert the laser beam after the beam sampler at 90° using a right-angle prism (RAP1).
Use another right-angle prism (RAP2) to allow the beam to pass through a variable neutral density filter (NDF2; OD = 0-4.0).
Direct the beam onto a multimode fiber (MMF).
Pass the laser beam through a fiber coupler (FC)-a combination of objectives (numerical aperture (NA): 0.25) and an XY translator.
Fix the fiber onto the scanning stage using an XY translator.
Place a plano-convex lens (L1) 25 mm away from the fiber output end to collimate the beam out of the fiber.
Pass the collimated beam through a conical lens with an apex angle of 130° to generate a ring-shaped beam.
Weakly focus the ring-shaped beam onto the subject using a homemade optical condenser (OC) with cone angles of 70° and 110° and with a hole in the center.
Place a 50 MHz ultrasonic transducer (UST) with an acoustic lens (AL) at the center of the homemade condenser.
Set the laser wavelength at 570 nm using an external controller.
Set the repetition rate of the laser at 5 kHz using the laser software.
Rotate the computer-controlled rotational stage by 90° to divert the laser beam onto an iris for reshaping.
Attenuate the laser beam placing a variable neutral density filter along the beam.
Focus the attenuated laser beam with a condenser lens (CL).
Pass the focused beam through a pinhole (PH) 75 mm away from the CL for spatial filtering.
Launch the spatially filtered beam onto a single-mode fiber using a single-mode fiber coupler (FC) consisting of a 0.1 NA objective to focus the light beam on to the SMF.
Adjust the fiber coupler to achieve maximum coupling efficiency.
Fix the fiber out onto the scanning stage using a slip plate (SP).
Place an achromatic lens (L2) 50 mm away from the single-mode fiber to collimate the laser beam.
Divert the collimated beam by 90° using a kinematic controllable elliptical mirror.
Place the achromatic lens used for focusing on a translation mount using a lens tube.
Pass the focusing beam through a homemade optoacoustic beam combiner consisting of a right-angled prism and a rhomboid prism, with a layer of silicon oil in between.
Attach an acoustic lens to provide acoustic focusing at the bottom of the rhomboid prism.
Place the ultrasonic transducer with a 50 MHz center frequency on top of the rhomboid prism using an epoxy layer for effective coupling.
Fix the homemade switchable plate to a 3-axis motorized stage tightly by screwing.
Attach the AR and OR cage system to the homemade plate using cage mounting brackets.
Slide the scan head on top of the imaging area.
Submerge the bottom part of the AR-OR-PAM scanner head in a water-filled acrylic tank for acoustic coupling.
Open an imaging window with a 7-cm diameter on the bottom plate of the tank and seal it with a polyethylene membrane for optical and acoustic transmission.
Align the ultrasound transducer using a pulse-echo amplifier and an oscilloscope.
Set the gain in the pulse echo amplifier to 24 dB in transmission/receiving mode.
Detect the backscattered signal from a glass slide inserted at the bottom of the water tank using an oscilloscope.
Move the Z-axis to maximize the amplitude of the pulse-echo signal on the oscilloscope.
Switch on the laser and connect the ultrasound transducer (UST) to two amplifiers with 24 dB fixed gain, using BNC cables.
Use the signal from the photodiode placed in front of the laser as a trigger for the data acquisition system.
Vary the distance between the conical lens and the optical condenser to maximize the amplitude of the photoacoustic signal generated from the test object.
Ensure that the optical and acoustic focuses are confocal by determining the maximum photoacoustic signal amplitude.
Loosen the screw of the scanning head and manually switch the scanning head from AR-PAM to OR-PAM.
Tighten the screws after switching the scanning head.
Dilute 0.1 mL of nanoparticle solution with an equal amount of water.
Distribute 0.1 mL of diluted nanoparticle solution on a cover slip and place it in contact with the polyethylene membrane under the tank.
Set the scan parameters for the AR-PAM and press the "scan" button to start raster scanning.
Set the scan parameters for the AR-PAM in the data acquisition software at 4 mm/s scanning speed.
Set the pulse repetition rate to 1 kHz.
Set the Y-scan range to 0.5 mm.
Set the X-scan range to 0.5 mm.
Set the step size in the x-direction to 4 µm.
Press the "scan" button to start raster scanning with AR-PAM.
Set the scan parameters for the OR-PAM at 2.5 mm/s scanning speed.
Set the pulse repetition rate to 5 kHz.
Set the Y-scan range to 0.5 mm.
Set the X-scan range to 0.5 mm.
Set the step size in the x-direction to 0.5 µm.
Ensure that data is continuously captured and stored on the computer during scanning.
Retrieve maximum amplitude projection (MAP) images from multiple B-scan data using image processing software.
Manually plot a line through the central region of a single nanoparticle image to obtain a point-spread function resembling a Gaussian curve.
Fit the obtained point-spread function with a Gaussian fit function using image processing software.
Measure the full width at half maximum (FWHM) to determine the lateral resolution.
Insert black tape obliquely onto sliced chicken tissue, attaching it to a metal plate for depth imaging.
Place the tissue with attached tape in the water tank.
Set scan parameters for AR-PAM into data acquisition software: 15 mm/s scanning speed, 1 kHz pulse repetition rate, 5 cm Y-scan range, and 0.1 mm X-scan range.
Set step size in the x-direction to 0.1 mm.
Press the "scan" button to capture a single B-scan image for maximum imaging depth determination.
Set the scan parameters for the OR-PAM and press the "scan" button to capture a single B-scan image to determine the maximum imaging depth.
Set the scanning speed to 15 mm/s in the velocity tab.
Set the pulse repetition rate to 5 kHz.
Set the Y-scan range to 2 cm.
Set the X-scan range to 0.1 mm.
Set the step size in the x-direction at 0.1 mm.
Use a female mouse with a bodyweight of 25 g and an age of 4 weeks.
Anesthetize the animal using a cocktail of ketamine (120 mg/kg) and xylazine (16 mg/kg) injected intraperitoneally.
Remove the hair from the animal ear using hair removal cream.
Wipe the area clean.
Cover the eye of the animal with a sterile ocular ointment to avoid any scattered laser beam falling onto the eyes.
Position the animal on a stage that also has a miniature plate to position the ear.
Maintain anesthesia with inhaled isoflurane (0.75% in 1 L/min oxygen) during the imaging period.
Clamp a pulse oximeter to the mouse leg or tail.
Monitor the physiological status.
Allow the imaging region to be in contact with the polyethylene membrane using ultrasound gel.
Set the scan parameters for the AR-PAM in the data acquisition software at "15" mm/s scanning speed.
Set the scan parameters for the AR-PAM in the data acquisition software at "1" kHz pulse repetition rate.
Set the scan parameters for the AR-PAM in the data acquisition software at "10" mm Y-scan range.
Set the scan parameters for the AR-PAM in the data acquisition software at "6" mm X-scan range.
Set the step size in the x-direction as "30" µm in the dx tab.
Press the "scan" button to start raster scanning with AR-PAM.
Switch the imaging head position from AR-PAM to OR-PAM.
Set the scan parameters for the OR-PAM in the data acquisition software at "15" mm/s scan speed.
Set the scan parameters for the OR-PAM in the data acquisition software at "5" kHz pulse repetition rate.
Set the scan parameters for the OR-PAM in the data acquisition software at "10" mm Y-scan range.
Set the scan parameters for the OR-PAM in the data acquisition software at "6" mm X-scan range.
Set the step size in the x-direction as "6" µm in the dx tab.
Press the "scan" button to start raster scanning with OR-PAM.
Retrieve the MAP images from the multiple B-scan data using image processing software.
Observe the animal throughout the entire imaging period.
